steps: Early aggressive IV fluid resuscitation (isotonic saline) to maintain high urine output — cornerstone to prevent AKI.
Monitor and treat hyperkalaemia and other electrolyte/acid-base disturbances; watch calcium/phosphate.
Treat the cause (relieve compression, stop offending drug, control seizures/agitation, manage hyperthermia).
Avoid nephrotoxins; consider urinary alkalinisation in selected cases (controversial).
Dialysis for refractory hyperkalaemia/acidosis/overload; watch for compartment syndrome.

drugRefs.dose: start ~1–2 L/h, then titrate to urine output 200–300 mL/h
drugRefs.freq: continuous, titrated to urine output and volume status
drugRefs.why: Early, aggressive isotonic fluids maintain renal perfusion and flush myoglobin, the single most effective measure to prevent pigment-induced AKI.

drugRefs.regimenLabel: Cardiac membrane stabilisation (hyperkalaemia with ECG changes)
drugRefs.dose: 10 mL of 10% IV over 5–10 min, repeat as needed
drugRefs.why: Stabilises the myocardium against hyperkalaemic arrhythmia; does not lower potassium.
Drives potassium intracellularly; give with glucose to avoid hypoglycaemia.

drugRefs.dose: 50 mL of 50% (25 g) IV with insulin
drugRefs.why: Prevents insulin-induced hypoglycaemia during potassium shifting.
Additional intracellular potassium shift; adjunct, not a substitute for insulin-glucose.

drugRefs.dose: isotonic (1.26%) infusion titrated to urine pH >6.5 (or 8.4% correction of severe acidosis)
drugRefs.why: May reduce myoglobin tubular toxicity but evidence is weak and it risks hypocalcaemia/alkalosis — reserve for selected cases and stop if no benefit.

decision.label: Aggressive IV fluids; monitor and treat hyperkalaemia

confirm: Muscle pain/weakness with markedly raised creatine kinase ± myoglobinuria (dark urine) and AKI; common after immobility, trauma, seizures, toxins, statins.
